title: Beyond Visible Spectrum: AI for Agriculture (AgVision AI)
why_relevant: Provides public context for the broader challenge theme (agriculture disease detection with beyond-RGB sensing) and helps triangulate modality expectations when Kaggle pages are partially inaccessible.
extracted_technique: Use multimodal fusion (RGB + multispectral/hyperspectral) with strong CV backbones and careful validation; emphasize spectral-spatial features.
query: Beyond Visible Spectrum AI for Agriculture 2026 Kaggle competition
takeaway: Public challenge pages confirm the multimodal remote-sensing framing; they do not reliably expose Kaggle evaluation/submission details, so local dataset inspection + notebook baseline remain the operational anchor.

title: SpectralFormer: Rethinking Hyperspectral Image Classification with Transformers
why_relevant: A strong, widely cited approach for learning spectral sequence structure in hyperspectral classification; useful for designing the HS branch or tokenization strategy.
extracted_technique: Group-wise spectral embeddings and transformer-style sequence modeling across neighboring bands to capture spectral locality beyond CNNs.
takeaway: For small-sample HSI classification, explicitly modeling spectral locality/sequences can outperform pure 2D CNNs; a lightweight variant (or PCA+CNN proxy) can be a pragmatic competition implementation.

title: HybridSN: Exploring 3D-2D CNN Feature Hierarchy for Hyperspectral Image Classification (implementation)
why_relevant: HybridSN-style 3D→2D spectral-spatial CNNs are a proven, implementable baseline for HS-only branches; can be ensembled with RGB/MS models for complementary gains.
extracted_technique: 3D convolutions over spectral stacks followed by 2D convolutions over spatial maps; optionally focal loss for imbalance/ कठिन samples.
takeaway: Hybrid 3D–2D CNN hierarchies are a practical way to extract spectral-spatial features from HS cubes; they are heavier than PCA+2D CNN but can improve robustness when blended.

title: A ConvNet for the 2020s (ConvNeXt)
why_relevant: ConvNeXt backbones (via timm) are strong transfer-learning foundations for RGB (and adaptable to MS/HS via in_chans or projectors), especially with limited labeled data.
extracted_technique: Modernized ConvNet design with transformer-like training/architecture choices; strong ImageNet transfer; easy to fine-tune.
takeaway: Use ConvNeXt variants as default encoders; for non-RGB channels, adapt first layer weights or learn a 1×1 projector, then fine-tune with heavy regularization on small datasets.
